request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change to a sheet now writes a line to the audit file, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass. Only the server changed; the screens already sent the signed-in user with every request.

- **How the lines are written:** I added `recordOnCommit` to `Audit.java`. It holds the line back until the database save has gone through, then appends it. If a change is refused or rolled back, by today's rules or any added later, it writes nothing.
- **People** (`PersonService`): adding a person writes `PERSON_ADDED` and editing one writes `PERSON_EDITED`, with `name` and `grade`. Editing a person didn't record who made the change before, so the server now passes the user through.
- **Claims** (`ClaimService`): adding a claim writes `CLAIM_ADDED` and editing one writes `CLAIM_EDITED`, with `person`, `amount` and `date`. The person is shown by their current name, the amount always has two decimals (`5.00`) and the date is yyyy-mm-dd. A claim left without a date is recorded with the sheet's today.

Saving an edit without changing any values still writes a `CLAIM_EDITED` line; one of the tests expects that.
